text: Read carefully the poem on page 3. The poet is alone in the family house now that her children
have grown up and left home. She listens to the sounds in her empty house.
How does the poet memorably convey her response to being alone?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• how she uses sounds to convey her feelings
• how she portrays her memories
• how she feels at the end of the poem.
Alone

Read carefully the following opening to a historical novel. It is set during the Second World War,
and the boy’s town is about to be invaded. He is trying to find a place of safety for himself and his
younger brother. He thinks the schoolmaster can help them.
How does the writer make this such a tense opening to the novel?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• how the writer portrays the town at daybreak
• how he conveys an atmosphere of growing tension
• how the writing makes the final two paragraphs dramatic.
He is out and running in the first grey of morning.

His brother grips him, small fists tight and fearful, and then already the boy is turning,
already he is running, making for the shelter of one of the town’s many alleyways – even
before he hears the rumbling of all the many vehicles following.
